tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

1	// 双发发布器（普通节点版）：一次调用同时发布 rosidl 与 protobuf 两路话题。
2	//
3	// ============================================================================
4	// 为什么需要这个封装，而不是在每个节点里写两个 publish
5	// ============================================================================
6	// 双发不是「多写一行 publish」那么简单，它有三个每次都必须处理对的细节：
7	//
8	//   1. 话题名派生。既有代码用 ResolveVehicleTopic 做 per-vehicle 派生，
9	//      proto 话题必须走同一套规则，否则多车场景下 __proto 只发全局名，
10	//      订阅方按车拿不到。这里统一交给调用方传「已解析好的 rosidl 话题名」，
11	//      内部只追加后缀，保证派生只做一次。
12	//
13	//   2. lifecycle 发布器的激活态。dispatcher_node 用的是
14	//      rclcpp_lifecycle::LifecyclePublisher，未激活时 publish 是静默空操作。
15	//      rosidl 侧靠 on_activate/on_deactivate 管理，proto 侧若不同步处理，
16	//      就会出现「节点 active 了但 proto 话题没数据」这种只在运行时可见的偏差。
17	//      ——这一半不在本文件里，见 proto_lifecycle_dual_publisher.hpp。
18	//
19	//   3. 总开关。过渡期必须能一键关掉 proto 侧（回滚、压测、排查），
20	//      而不必改代码或重新构建。开关做成构造参数，由节点参数注入。
21	//
22	// ============================================================================
23	// 为什么拆成两个头文件 / 两个类
24	// ============================================================================
25	// rclcpp 的 Publisher 有两种类型（普通 / lifecycle），且 lifecycle 版在
26	// rclcpp_lifecycle 包里。若在同一个类里用模板参数二选一，头文件就必然
27	// include <rclcpp_lifecycle/lifecycle_node.hpp>，让 chassis_driver /
28	// path_tracker / safety_gate / link_health 这四个**根本不是 lifecycle 节点**
29	// 的可执行目标凭空多一条 rclcpp_lifecycle 依赖——多一个包要在
30	// ament_target_dependencies 里声明，还得保证运行时能加载。
31	//
32	// 拆开之后：本文件只依赖 rclcpp，普通节点零成本；lifecycle 变体单独一份，
33	// 只有 dispatcher_node 引入。两者共用 ProtoTopicName 与 ProjectRosidlToProto，
34	// 所以两路投影逻辑仍只有一份实现。
35	#ifndef AMR_DISPATCHER_ROS__PROTO_DUAL_PUBLISHER_HPP_
36	#define AMR_DISPATCHER_ROS__PROTO_DUAL_PUBLISHER_HPP_
37	
38	#include <memory>
39	#include <string>
40	#include <type_traits>
41	
42	#include <rclcpp/rclcpp.hpp>
43	
44	#include "amr_dispatcher_ros/proto_projection.hpp"
45	
46	// 让 create_publisher<ProtoT> 能通过 rclcpp 的消息类型检查。
47	#include "amr_dispatcher_proto/register_all_types.hpp"
48	
49	namespace amr_dispatcher_ros
50	{
51	
52	/// proto 话题名的后缀。
53	///
54	/// 选 `_proto` 而不是 `/proto/` 子命名空间：ROS 话题名里 `/proto/xxx` 会变成
55	/// 另一个层级，按前缀做 ros2 topic list 通配时会与既有话题分散；后缀形式
56	/// 让 `/chassis/link_health` 与 `/chassis/link_health_proto` 在列表里相邻，
57	/// 运维一眼能看出配对关系。
58	inline constexpr const char * kProtoTopicSuffix = "_proto";
59	
60	/// 由 rosidl 话题名派生 proto 话题名。
61	///
62	/// 入参必须已经是**解析后的最终话题名**（即 ResolveVehicleTopic 的输出），
63	/// 这样 per-vehicle 派生只发生一次，不会出现 `/plan/amr_01_proto` 与
64	/// `/plan_proto/amr_01` 两种不一致的结果。
65	inline std::string ProtoTopicName(const std::string & rosidl_topic)
66	{
67	  return rosidl_topic + kProtoTopicSuffix;
68	}
69	
70	/// 把 rosidl 消息投影成 proto 消息。
71	///
72	/// 用 if constexpr 做类型分发而不是要求 ProtoT 提供静态 Project 方法：
73	/// protobuf 生成的类不接受注入，而投影函数是自由函数，只能在此做分派。
74	/// 分支写错会在编译期落到 else 的 static_assert，不会静默走错路径。
75	///
76	/// 本函数被普通版与 lifecycle 版两个双发器共用，所以投影只此一份。
77	template<typename RosidlMsgT, typename ProtoT>
78	void ProjectRosidlToProto(const RosidlMsgT & in, ProtoT * out)
79	{
80	  using amr_dispatcher_interfaces::msg::ChassisLinkHealth;
81	  using amr_dispatcher_interfaces::msg::DispatcherState;
82	  using amr_dispatcher_interfaces::msg::MissionEvent;
83	  using amr_dispatcher_interfaces::msg::SafetyState;
84	  using amr_dispatcher_interfaces::msg::TopologyState;
85	  using amr_dispatcher_interfaces::msg::TrackingError;
86	
87	  if constexpr (std::is_same_v<RosidlMsgT, ChassisLinkHealth> &&
88	    std::is_same_v<ProtoT, amr_dispatcher::proto::ChassisLinkHealth>)
89	  {
90	    proto_projection::ProjectChassisLinkHealth(in, out);
91	  } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<RosidlMsgT, TrackingError> &&
92	    std::is_same_v<ProtoT, amr_dispatcher::proto::TrackingError>)
93	  {
94	    proto_projection::ProjectTrackingError(in, out);
95	  } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<RosidlMsgT, DispatcherState> &&
96	    std::is_same_v<ProtoT, amr_dispatcher::proto::DispatcherState>)
97	  {
98	    proto_projection::ProjectDispatcherState(in, out);
99	  } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<RosidlMsgT, SafetyState> &&
100	    std::is_same_v<ProtoT, amr_dispatcher::proto::SafetyState>)
101	  {
102	    proto_projection::ProjectSafetyState(in, out);
103	  } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<RosidlMsgT, TopologyState> &&
104	    std::is_same_v<ProtoT, amr_dispatcher::proto::TopologyState>)
105	  {
106	    proto_projection::ProjectTopologyState(in, out);
107	  } else if constexpr (std::is_same_v<RosidlMsgT, MissionEvent> &&
108	    std::is_same_v<ProtoT, amr_dispatcher::proto::MissionEvent>)
109	  {
110	    proto_projection::ProjectMissionEvent(in, out);
111	  } else {
112	    static_assert(
113	      !std::is_same_v<RosidlMsgT, RosidlMsgT>,
114	      "no proto projection registered for this message pair; "
115	      "add it to proto_projection.{hpp,cpp} and to this dispatch chain");
116	  }
117	}
118	
119	/// 双发器：持有 proto 发布器，提供从 rosidl 消息投影并发布的单一入口。
120	///
121	/// 模板参数 ProtoT 必须是已在 register_all_types.hpp 注册过的类型。
122	/// 普通 rclcpp::Node 用本类；lifecycle 节点用 ProtoLifecycleDualPublisher。
123	template<typename RosidlMsgT, typename ProtoT>
124	class ProtoDualPublisher
125	{
126	public:
127	  /// 构造即创建发布器，也立即可发——普通发布器没有激活态。
128	  ///
129	  /// \param node        宿主节点（用于 create_publisher 与日志）
130	  /// \param rosidl_name 已解析的 rosidl 话题名（proto 名由它派生）
131	  /// \param qos_depth   QoS 深度。两侧必须一致：若 proto 侧深度更小，
132	  ///                    突发时会先丢 proto 帧，一致性检查器会报「proto 缺帧」
133	  ///                    而不是「消息不一致」，掩盖真正的问题。
134	  /// \param enabled     总开关。false 时完全不创建发布器，
135	  ///                    因此也不会在 DDS 里留下一个空话题。
136	  ProtoDualPublisher(
137	    rclcpp::Node * node, const std::string & rosidl_name, std::size_t qos_depth, bool enabled)
138	  : rosidl_topic_(rosidl_name),
139	    proto_topic_(ProtoTopicName(rosidl_name)),
140	    enabled_(enabled)
141	  {
142	    if (!enabled_) {
143	      return;
144	    }
145	    pub_ = node->create_publisher<ProtoT>(proto_topic_, rclcpp::QoS(qos_depth));
146	  }
147	
148	  /// 是否真正启用了 proto 侧。调用方用它决定是否值得构造 proto 消息。
149	  bool enabled() const {return static_cast<bool>(pub_);}
150	
151	  const std::string & proto_topic() const {return proto_topic_;}
152	
153	  /// 从 rosidl 消息投影并发布。未启用时为空操作。
154	  ///
155	  /// 返回是否真的投递到底层发布器，便于调用方在测试中断言。
156	  bool Publish(const RosidlMsgT & msg)
157	  {
158	    if (!pub_) {
159	      return false;
160	    }
161	    ProtoT proto_msg;
162	    ProjectRosidlToProto(msg, &proto_msg);
163	    pub_->publish(proto_msg);
164	    return true;
165	  }
166	
167	private:
168	  std::string rosidl_topic_;
169	  std::string proto_topic_;
170	  bool enabled_{false};
171	  typename rclcpp::Publisher<ProtoT>::SharedPtr pub_;
172	};
173	
174	}  // namespace amr_dispatcher_ros
175	
176	#endif  // AMR_DISPATCHER_ROS__PROTO_DUAL_PUBLISHER_HPP_

Now I have a clear picture. Let me think about the design decision for Phase3.

The key question: should consumers actually *switch* to proto topics, or should they have a runtime toggle?

Let me think carefully. The plan says Phase3 is "消费者迁移" - consumers migrate to read proto topics. But there's a fundamental design consideration:

1. Internal consumers (nodes inside the same project) currently subscribe to rosidl topics with C++ type safety. Migrating them to proto means:
 - They lose compile-time type checking on the message (well, they get proto generated types, which is typed too)
 - They must deserialize protobuf from CDR - They lose `ros2 topic echo` debuggability for those consumers' inputs2. The value of migrating internal consumers is questionable — the whole point of protobuf is cross-language/external consumption. Internal C++ consumers gain little and lose tooling.

But the user said "把剩余的迁移计划都完整做了吧" — complete all remaining plan items.

I need to be honest about this. Let me think about what's actually achievable and correct:

**Phase3 options:**
- (A) Hard-switch all consumers to proto topics only. This breaks the "dual publish observation period" concept and removes rollback ability.
- (B) Add a symmetric `ProtoDualSubscriber` that subscribes to BOTH, with a `proto_dual_subscribe` parameter selecting source, defaulting to rosidl. This gives a runtime toggle, keeps rollback, and satisfies "consumer migration" incrementally.

(B) is clearly right and mirrors the publisher design. The parameter name should probably be `proto_dual_subscribe` with values... hmm. Actually let me think about naming symmetry. Publisher uses `proto_dual_publish` (bool). For subscriber, a bool `proto_dual_subscribe` would mean "also subscribe proto" — but that's not quite the semantic. The semantic is "which source do I read from".

Let me think about what's actually most useful and least risky:
- `proto_topic_source`: `"rosidl"` (default) | `"proto"`. Runtime switchable? ROS params are read at configure time typically. For a runtime toggle you'd need a parameter callback. Simpler: read at construction.

Actually, let me reconsider. There's a much more important consideration I should check: **is there any actual benefit/necessity?**

Let me think about what's genuinely valuable here:

=== proto CMakeLists 关键段 ===
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(amr_dispatcher_proto)

# C++17 是硬性要求：
#   - protobuf 3.21 的 CMake 集成要求 17
#   - 本包的类型分发依赖 if constexpr（SILENT 分支）
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
find_package(rclcpp REQUIRED)

# ament_get_python_install_dir() 提供 PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR，用于把 pybind11
# 扩展装到 site-packages（而不是 ROS 的可执行文件目录 lib/<pkg>）。
find_package(ament_cmake_python REQUIRED)

# protobuf 用 CONFIG 模式优先，找不到再退回 MODULE。
# Ubuntu 24.04 / protobuf 3.21 装的是 Module 模式（FindProtobuf.cmake）。
# 若将来升级到 protobuf 4.x（开始提供 CONFIG 模式），这里仍然兼容。
find_package(Protobuf REQUIRED)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# protobuf 代码生成
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 所有 proto 放在同一个 PROTO_PATH 下，互相 import 才能解析。
set(PROTO_SRC_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/proto)

set(PROTO_FILES
  ${PROTO_SRC_DIR}/common.proto
  ${PROTO_SRC_DIR}/chassis.proto
  ${PROTO_SRC_DIR}/dispatcher.proto
  ${PROTO_SRC_DIR}/safety.proto
)

# 生成到 build 目录，不污染源码树。
set(PROTO_GEN_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated)
file(MAKE_DIRECTORY ${PROTO_GEN_DIR})

# 让构建期的 #include 路径与安装后的**逐字相同**。
#
# 问题：protoc 生成的 .pb.cc 之间用平铺名互相包含（`#include "common.pb.h"`），
# 而安装后位于 include/amr_dispatcher_proto/generated/common.pb.h。若下游包
# 按安装路径写 include，构建期就找不到；反之亦然——同一份头文件两套写法，
# 协作方必然记错。
#
# 解法：构建目录里造一个与安装同形的 include 根，用符号链接指回平铺目录。
# 于是 `amr_dispatcher_proto/generated/chassis.pb.h` 在构建期与安装后都成立，
# 且不产生第二份实体文件（不会出现两份头内容不一致的隐患）。
#
# 平台约束：项目仅支持 Linux（见 docker/Dockerfile.jazzy），符号链接可用。
set(PROTO_INCLUDE_ROOT ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/include)
file(MAKE_DIRECTORY ${PROTO_INCLUDE_ROOT}/amr_dispatcher_proto)
file(CREATE_LINK ${PROTO_GEN_DIR}
  ${PROTO_INCLUDE_ROOT}/amr_dispatcher_proto/generated
  SYMBOLIC)

set(PROTO_GENERATED_SRCS)
set(PROTO_GENERATED_HDRS)

foreach(proto_file ${PROTO_FILES})
...
endif()

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 冒烟自检（骨架验证，不是正式测试）
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
add_executable(proto_smoke_test src/smoke_test.cpp)
target_link_libraries(proto_smoke_test ${PROJECT_NAME})
ament_target_dependencies(proto_smoke_test rclcpp)

install(TARGETS proto_smoke_test DESTINATION lib/${PROJECT_NAME})

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 安装
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
install(
  DIRECTORY include/
  DESTINATION include
)

install(
  TARGETS ${PROJECT_NAME}
  EXPORT export_${PROJECT_NAME}
  ARCHIVE DESTINATION lib
  LIBRARY DESTINATION lib
  RUNTIME DESTINATION bin
)

# .proto 也装上：下游包若要做跨语言（Python/Java）桥接会需要。
install(
  DIRECTORY proto/
  DESTINATION share/${PROJECT_NAME}/proto
)

# 生成的 .pb.h 必须安装，否则下游包 include 不到。
install(
  FILES ${PROTO_GENERATED_HDRS}
  DESTINATION include/amr_dispatcher_proto/generated
)

ament_export_include_directories(include)
ament_export_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME})
ament_export_dependencies(
  rclcpp
  Protobuf
  fastcdr

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
project(amr_dispatcher_ros)

if(NOT CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD)
  set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
  set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
endif()

find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
find_package(rclcpp REQUIRED)
find_package(rclcpp_lifecycle REQUIRED)
find_package(rclcpp_action REQUIRED)
find_package(std_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(geometry_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(nav_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(sensor_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(visualization_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(yaml-cpp REQUIRED)
find_package(tf2 REQUIRED)
find_package(tf2_ros REQUIRED)
find_package(tf2_geometry_msgs REQUIRED)
find_package(hardware_interface REQUIRED)
find_package(pluginlib REQUIRED)
find_package(amr_dispatcher_core REQUIRED)
find_package(amr_dispatcher_interfaces REQUIRED)
find_package(amr_dispatcher_bt REQUIRED)
# 阶段 2：protobuf 双发（见 PROTOBUF_MIGRATION_PLAN.md §3.3）。
#
# 这里是**硬依赖**，不学 nav2_msgs / Paho 那样 QUIET 跳过。理由：
# 双发是阶段 2 的正式功能，静默降级会得到一个「构建成功但 proto 话题根本不存在」
# 的镜像，而这种缺失只有在运维真的去订阅时才暴露——比构建期直接失败更贵。
# 部署侧依赖已在 docker/Dockerfile.jazzy 与 CI 中显式安装。
find_package(amr_dispatcher_proto REQUIRED)
# 显式 find Protobuf：下游目标的 pb.h 会 include <google/protobuf/*>，
# 需要 Protobuf_INCLUDE_DIRS。见下面 amr_dispatcher_proto_dual 的注释。
find_package(Protobuf REQUIRED)
# nav2_msgs 可选：镜像缺包时 QUIET 跳过，桥接节点 Nav2 分支条件编译，容器构建永不因 Nav2 挂掉
find_package(nav2_msgs QUIET)
# Eclipse Paho MQTT C++ 可选（Task 4 vda5050_gateway_node）：镜像缺包时跳过该目标编译，
# full_system.launch.py 默认 use_vda5050=false 不引用该可执行文件，构建永不因缺 Paho 挂掉。
# I1：C++ 头/库与 C 库三者齐备才启用——C 库是条件链接（pp3 依赖 MQTTAsync_* 符号，
# 半装环境会编译通过再在链接期报 undefined reference）；NAMES 只列异步变体
# （同步 3c/3cs 无 MQTTAsync_*，链上也无法满足 pp3 的依赖）。
find_path(PAHO_MQTTPP_INCLUDE_DIR NAMES mqtt/async_client.h)
find_library(PAHO_MQTTPP_LIBRARY NAMES paho-mqttpp3)
find_library(PAHO_MQTT_LIBRARY NAMES paho-mqtt3as paho-mqtt3a)
if(PAHO_MQTTPP_INCLUDE_DIR AND PAHO_MQTTPP_LIBRARY AND PAHO_MQTT_LIBRARY)
  set(AMR_HAVE_PAHO_MQTT TRUE)
else()
  set(AMR_HAVE_PAHO_MQTT FALSE)
  message(WARNING "未找到 Eclipse Paho MQTT C++ (libpaho-mqttpp-dev) 或异步 C 客户端库 (libpaho-mqtt-dev)，跳过 vda5050_gateway_node 编译")
endif()

# 2.0 proto 投影层（阶段 2 双发的地基）
#
# 做成共享库而不是 header-only，原因有两条：
#   1. 投影实现在 .cpp 里（见 proto_projection.cpp）。7 个消息 × 每字段一行，
#      放头文件会被 8 个可执行目标各编译一次，构建时间线性膨胀。
#   2. 单测（test_proto_projection）需要链接同一份实现来验证字段完整性，
#      共享库让「测的就是用的」成立；header-only 也能做到，但容易在
#      不同 TU 里出现 ODR 违规的弱符号。
add_library(amr_dispatcher_proto_projection SHARED
  src/proto_projection.cpp
)
target_include_directories(amr_dispatcher_proto_projection PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(amr_dispatcher_proto_projection
  rclcpp
  std_msgs
  amr_dispatcher_interfaces
  amr_dispatcher_proto
)

# 双发所需的**全部**编译期依赖，打包成一个 INTERFACE 目标。
#
# 为什么需要这一层：调用 create_publisher<ProtoT> 的节点必须同时拿到
#   - amr_dispatcher_proto 的 include（register_all_types.hpp、protobuf_typesupport.hpp）
#   - 生成的 pb.h 所在目录（由 amr_dispatcher_proto 的 include 导出覆盖）
#   - Protobuf 自身的头文件（pb.h 内部 include <google/protobuf/*>）
#   - fastcdr（protobuf_typesupport.hpp include <fastcdr/Cdr.h>）
# 后两项 amr_dispatcher_proto 通过 ament_export_dependencies 导出，但
# ament_export_dependencies 只负责让 find_package 成功，不会自动把
# Protobuf_INCLUDE_DIRS 塞进下游目标。漏掉它会在下游报
# "google/protobuf/message.h: No such file or directory"，而错误位置在
# proto 包的头文件里，指向性很差。
add_library(amr_dispatcher_proto_dual INTERFACE)
target_link_libraries(amr_dispatcher_proto_dual INTERFACE
  amr_dispatcher_proto_projection
  ${Protobuf_LIBRARIES}
)
target_include_directories(amr_dispatcher_proto_dual INTERFACE
  ${Protobuf_INCLUDE_DIRS}
)

# 1. chassis_driver_node

add_executable(chassis_driver_node
  src/chassis_driver_node.cpp
)
target_include_directories(chassis_driver_node PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(chassis_driver_node
  rclcpp
  geometry_msgs
  nav_msgs
  sensor_msgs
  tf2
  tf2_ros
  tf2_geometry_msgs
  amr_dispatcher_core
  amr_dispatcher_interfaces
)
# 阶段 2 双发：ChassisLinkHealth -> /chassis/link_health_proto
target_link_libraries(chassis_driver_node amr_dispatcher_proto_dual)

# 2. dispatcher_node
add_executable(dispatcher_node
  src/dispatcher_node.cpp
)
target_include_directories(dispatcher_node PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(dispatcher_node
  rclcpp
  rclcpp_lifecycle
  rclcpp_action
  nav_msgs
  geometry_msgs
  sensor_msgs
  amr_dispatcher_core
  amr_dispatcher_interfaces
)
# 行为树编排层：订单路由、出队派发门控、恢复与结果决策
target_link_libraries(dispatcher_node amr_dispatcher_bt::amr_dispatcher_bt)
# 阶段 2 双发：DispatcherState / MissionEvent / TopologyState -> *_proto
# 注意：dispatcher_node 是 lifecycle 节点，双发器用的是 ProtoLifecycleDualPublisher
# （proto 侧跟随 on_activate/on_deactivate），编译期依赖与普通版完全相同。
target_link_libraries(dispatcher_node amr_dispatcher_proto_dual)


# 2.1 navigate_sequence_bridge_node
# /navigate_sequence action server：fallback 转 /plan（复用 path_tracker 链），
# use_nav2:=true 时条件编译走 Nav2 navigate_to_pose（镜像缺 nav2_msgs 则自动降级）
add_executable(navigate_sequence_bridge_node
  src/navigate_sequence_bridge_node.cpp
)
target_include_directories(navigate_sequence_bridge_node PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(navigate_sequence_bridge_node
  rclcpp
  rclcpp_action
  nav_msgs
  geometry_msgs
  amr_dispatcher_interfaces
)
if(nav2_msgs_FOUND)
  target_compile_definitions(navigate_sequence_bridge_node PRIVATE AMR_HAVE_NAV2_MSGS)
  ament_target_dependencies(navigate_sequence_bridge_node nav2_msgs)
endif()

# 3. safety_gate_node
add_executable(safety_gate_node
  src/safety_gate_node.cpp
)
target_include_directories(safety_gate_node PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(safety_gate_node
  rclcpp
  geometry_msgs
  std_msgs
  amr_dispatcher_core
  amr_dispatcher_interfaces
)
# 阶段 2 双发：SafetyState -> /safety/state_proto
target_link_libraries(safety_gate_node amr_dispatcher_proto_dual)

# 4. path_tracker_node
add_executable(path_tracker_node
  src/path_tracker_node.cpp
)
target_include_directories(path_tracker_node PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(path_tracker_node
  rclcpp
  geometry_msgs
  nav_msgs
  tf2
  tf2_geometry_msgs
  amr_dispatcher_core
  amr_dispatcher_interfaces
)
# 阶段 2 双发：TrackingError -> /tracking/error_proto（全项目频率最高的双发点）
target_link_libraries(path_tracker_node amr_dispatcher_proto_dual)

# 5. link_health_publisher
add_executable(link_health_publisher
  src/link_health_publisher.cpp
)
target_include_directories(link_health_publisher PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(link_health_publisher
  rclcpp
  amr_dispatcher_core
  amr_dispatcher_interfaces
)
# 阶段 2 双发：/system/aggregated_link_health_proto
target_link_libraries(link_health_publisher amr_dispatcher_proto_dual)

# 6. dispatcher_visualizer_node
add_executable(dispatcher_visualizer_node
  src/dispatcher_visualizer_node.cpp
)
target_include_directories(dispatcher_visualizer_node PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(dispatcher_visualizer_node
  rclcpp
  geometry_msgs
  std_msgs
  visualization_msgs
  amr_dispatcher_core
  amr_dispatcher_interfaces
)
target_link_libraries(dispatcher_visualizer_node yaml-cpp)

# 7. lifecycle_coordinator_node
add_executable(lifecycle_coordinator_node
  src/lifecycle_coordinator_node.cpp
)
target_include_directories(lifecycle_coordinator_node PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(lifecycle_coordinator_node
  rclcpp
  lifecycle_msgs
  std_msgs
  amr_dispatcher_interfaces
)

# 8. map_ingest_node（Task 8）：/map -> 核心库算法流水线（安全空间腐蚀、
# 骨架细化、受保护剪枝、拓扑构建）-> 原子写出 stations.yaml + 拓扑 Marker。
add_executable(map_ingest_node
  src/map_ingest_node.cpp
)
target_include_directories(map_ingest_node PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(map_ingest_node
  rclcpp

  geometry_msgs
  std_msgs

# yaml-cpp：解析 markers_file 的 anchors 段（与 dispatcher_visualizer 同一链接方式）
target_link_libraries(map_ingest_node yaml-cpp)

# 8.1 vda5050_gateway_node（Task 4）：VDA 5050 <-> ROS 2 MQTT 薄壳网关。
# MQTT 类型封装在 .cpp（pimpl），核心库 amr_dispatcher_core 保持零 MQTT 依赖（Spec §1 铁律）；
# 仅在检测到 Paho 时编译（见文件头 AMR_HAVE_PAHO_MQTT 判定）
if(AMR_HAVE_PAHO_MQTT)
  add_executable(vda5050_gateway_node
    src/vda5050_gateway_node.cpp
  )

  )

  # 三元守卫已保证 C 异步库存在；显式链接 C 客户端，

  target_link_libraries(vda5050_gateway_node
    ${PAHO_MQTTPP_LIBRARY}
    ${PAHO_MQTT_LIBRARY}
  )
endif()

# 6. ros2_control hardware plugin
add_library(amr_chassis_hardware_interface SHARED
  src/chassis_hardware_interface.cpp
)

target_include_directories(amr_chassis_hardware_interface PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
)
ament_target_dependencies(amr_chassis_hardware_interface
  rclcpp
  hardware_interface
  pluginlib
  amr_dispatcher_core
  amr_dispatcher_interfaces
)
pluginlib_export_plugin_description_file(hardware_interface chassis_hardware_interface.xml)

# 单元测试：可抽离的纯逻辑（B1 周期发布判定 / B3 航点位姿 / B4 任务戳记）

if(BUILD_TESTING)
  find_package(GTest REQUIRED)
  include(GoogleTest)
  enable_testing()

  add_library(amr_dispatcher_ros_helpers INTERFACE)
  target_include_directories(amr_dispatcher_ros_helpers INTERFACE
    $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
    $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
  )
  ament_target_dependencies(amr_dispatcher_ros_helpers INTERFACE
    geometry_msgs
    amr_dispatcher_core
  )

  # 纯逻辑单测：只依赖 amr_dispatcher_ros_helpers（rclcpp/几何/cored 的薄封装）
  set(ROS_UNIT_TESTS
    test_safety_publish_decision
    test_nav_pose_builder
    test_mission_identity
    test_report_freshness
    test_assignment_dispatch_decision
    test_chassis_fault
  )
  foreach(test_name IN LISTS ROS_UNIT_TESTS)
    set(test_src "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/test/${test_name}.cpp")

        amr_dispatcher_ros_helpers GTest::gtest GTest::gtest_main)

  # 阶段 2 双发的投影层单测：需要链接**同一份** amr_dispatcher_proto_projection

  # 全部编译期依赖（protobuf 头文件、pb.h、typesupport）；把它塞进通用循环会

  if(EXISTS "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/test/test_proto_projection.cpp")
    add_executable(test_proto_projection
      "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/test/test_proto_projection.cpp")
    target_link_libraries(test_proto_projection PRIVATE
      amr_dispatcher_proto_dual GTest::gtest GTest::gtest_main)
    gtest_discover_tests(test_proto_projection)

  # L2 契约测试：真进程 + 真服务调用（不再是 assertTrue(True)）。

   **Design decision reached (the main output of this segment): Phase 3 will be a transport-layer switch, not a native proto rewrite.**

   Rationale, stated explicitly: converting 8 consumer files to natively consume protobuf would mean rewriting 60+ field-access sites across the safety gate, the dispatcher state machine, and REST serialization (`rest_gateway` alone has ~40 references across `latest_state_`/`latest_safety_`/`latest_link_`/`recent_events_`). That would both risk behavior drift and destroy the very reference basis that makes the plan's "每个消费者迁移后观察一个版本周期" meaningful. Instead:

   - Add a `ProtoDualSubscriber` that subscribes to `<topic>_proto`, receives a protobuf message, **reverse-projects it back into the rosidl message type**, and invokes the node's existing rosidl callback unchanged.
   - Controlled by a `proto_dual_subscribe` runtime parameter mirroring `proto_dual_publish`, so each consumer can be flipped independently (matches the plan's per-consumer rollout).
   - Verified this is safe: the only method ever called on any of these subscription handles is `tracking_error_sub_.reset()` at `dispatcher_node.cpp:785`; all others are keep-alive-only, so a bridge wrapper can own the handle.

   **Forward-projection lossiness analyzed** — reverse projection is safe because real producers only emit closed-set values:
   - `tier`: `chassis_driver_node.cpp:516/519/522/526` and `link_health_publisher.cpp:105/107/109/111` write only HEALTHY/DEGRADED/CRITICAL/UNKNOWN.

   - `command_delivery_rate == -1.0` sentinel → `valid=false`; reverse must reconstruct `-1.0`.
   - Reverse rule for enums: known enum → canonical string via `ToTierString`/`ToSeverityString`; `UNKNOWN` → use `*_text` if non-empty, else `"UNKNOWN"`.

   **Unresolved dependency-placement question (the immediate blocker for writing code):**
   - The reverse projection must be linkable from both `amr_dispatcher_ros` and `amr_dispatcher_tools`.
   - `amr_dispatcher_tools` must NOT depend on `amr_dispatcher_ros` (that would drag in hardware_interface, pluginlib, rclcpp_action, amr_dispatcher_bt).
   - `amr_dispatcher_ros` has **no `ament_export_*` at all**, so it exports nothing downstream — the existing `amr_dispatcher_proto_projection` lib is unreachable from tools.
   - `amr_dispatcher_proto` does not (and arguably should not) depend on `amr_dispatcher_interfaces`; adding it would invert the layering of a package designed to be message-agnostic.
   - Options under consideration: (a) a new thin package (e.g. `amr_dispatcher_proto_bridge`) — cost: must sync the four hardcoded build-entrypoint package lists (CI ×2, `docker/entrypoint.server.sh`, `scripts/build.sh`), a documented trap from memory `build-entry-package-lists.md`; (b) place the header-only reverse projection in a package both already depend on and extend that package's exports.

I cannot verify whether any third party subscribes on a host machine. #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

DIR="$( cd "$( dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" )" >/dev/null 2>&1 && pwd )"
ROOT_DIR="$DIR/.."

echo "=== Building amr_dispatcher_core (Standalone CMake) ==="
cmake -S "$ROOT_DIR/src/amr_dispatcher_core" -B "$ROOT_DIR/build/core" \
      -DBUILD_TESTING=ON -DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS="-std=c++20" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release
cmake --build "$ROOT_DIR/build/core" -j$(nproc)

echo "=== Running Core Unit Tests ==="
ctest --test-dir "$ROOT_DIR/build/core" --output-on-failure

if [ -f "/opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash" ]; then
  echo "=== Sourcing ROS 2 Jazzy and building with colcon ==="
  # 必须在此**临时**关闭 -u：ROS 的 setup.bash 会引用未定义变量
  # （实测报 `AMENT_TRACE_SETUP_FILES: unbound variable`），在 `set -u`
  # 下 source 直接失败。这个坑只在「宿主机装了 ROS 且真的走到这一支」时出现，
  # 而 CI 的 core job 与无 ROS 的开发机都会跳过这一支，所以长期没被发现。
  set +u
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
  set -u
  cd "$ROOT_DIR"
  # --base-paths src 不可省：仓库根目录有一个 CMakeLists.txt，colcon 会把它
  # 当成包 amr_dispatcher_workspace 并**忽略 src/ 下所有真实包**。
  # 实测：不带该参数时 `colcon list` 只输出 amr_dispatcher_workspace，
  # 构建"成功"但 install/ 里一个 amr_dispatcher_* 都没有——这是静默失败，
  # 比报错更危险。用法与 docker/entrypoint.server.sh 保持一致。
  colcon build --base-paths src --symlink-install
else
  echo "[INFO] ROS 2 Jazzy not found in host environment. Colcon build skipped (run inside docker if needed)."
fi

echo "=== Build Complete ==="

Refuse requests for destructive techniques, DoS attacks, mass targeting, supply chain compromise, or detection evasion for malicious purposes.  - Prefer the dedicated file/search tools over shell commands when one fits. Independent tool calls can run in parallel in one response.
 - Reference code as `file_path:line_number` — it's clickable.
Write code that reads like the surrounding code: match its comment density, naming, and idiom.

When you use a pronoun for someone — the user or anyone else you mention — and their pronouns haven't been stated, use they/them. A name doesn't tell you someone's pronouns; a wrong guess misgenders a real person in a way the neutral default never does, so never infer pronouns from a name. This applies to all user-visible text, including visible thinking.

For actions that are hard to reverse or outward-facing, confirm first unless durably authorized or explicitly told to proceed without asking; approval in one context doesn't extend to the next. Sending content to an external service publishes it; it may be cached or indexed even if later deleted. Before deleting or overwriting, look at the target. Report outcomes faithfully: if tests fail, say so with the output; if a step was skipped, say that; when something is done and verified, state it plainly without hedging.

# Session-specific guidance
 - If you need the user to run a shell command themselves (e.g., an interactive login like `gcloud auth login`), suggest they type `! <command>` in the prompt — the `!` prefix runs the command in this session so its output lands directly in the conversation.
 - When the user types `/<skill-name>`, invoke it via Skill. Only use skills listed in the user-invocable skills section — don't guess.

# Memory

You have a persistent file-based memory at `/home/ubuntu/.claude/projects/-home-ubuntu------amr-dispatcher/memory/`. This directory already exists — write to it directly with the Write tool (do not run mkdir or check for its existence). Each memory is one file holding one fact, with frontmatter:

- Users will always be able to select "Other" to provide custom text input
- Use multiSelect: true to allow multiple answers to be selected for a question
- If you recommend a specific option, make that the first option in the list and add "(Recommended)" at the end of the label

Plan mode note: To switch into plan mode, use EnterPlanMode (not this tool). Once in plan mode, use this tool to clarify requirements or choose between approaches BEFORE finalizing your plan. Do NOT use this tool to ask "Is my plan ready?", "Should I proceed?", or otherwise reference "the plan" in questions — the user cannot see the plan until you call ExitPlanMode for approval.

  "remind me at 2:30pm today to check the deploy" → cron: "30 14 <today_dom> <today_month> *", recurring: false
  "tomorrow morning, run the smoke test" → cron: "57 8 <tomorrow_dom> <tomorrow_month> *", recurring: false

For "every N minutes" / "every hour" / "weekdays at 9am" requests:
  "*/5 * * * *" (every 5 min), "0 * * * *" (hourly), "0 9 * * 1-5" (weekdays at 9am local)

## Avoid the :00 and :30 minute marks when the task allows it

Every user who asks for "9am" gets `0 9`, and every user who asks for "hourly" gets `0 *` — which means requests from across the planet land on the API at the same instant. When the user's request is approximate, pick a minute that is NOT 0 or 30:
  "every morning around 9" → "57 8 * * *" or "3 9 * * *" (not "0 9 * * *")
  "hourly" → "7 * * * *" (not "0 * * * *")
  "in an hour or so, remind me to..." → pick whatever minute you land on, don't round

By default (durable: false) the job lives only in this Claude session — nothing is written to disk, and the job is gone when Claude exits. Pass durable: true to write to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json so the job survives restarts. Only use durable: true when the user explicitly asks for the task to persist ("keep doing this every day", "set this up permanently"). Most "remind me in 5 minutes" / "check back in an hour" requests should stay session-only.

Jobs only fire while the REPL is idle (not mid-query). Durable jobs persist to .claude/scheduled_tasks.json and survive session restarts — on next launch they resume automatically. Picking an off-minute is still the bigger lever.

Recurring tasks auto-expire after 7 days — they fire one final time, then are deleted. This bounds session lifetime. Tell the user about the 7-day limit when scheduling recurring jobs.

tools.name: EnterPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool proactively when you're about to start a non-trivial implementation task. Getting user sign-off on your approach before writing code prevents wasted effort and ensures alignment. This tool transitions you into plan mode where you can explore the codebase and design an implementation approach for user approval.

## When to Use This Tool

**Prefer using EnterPlanMode** for implementation tasks unless they're simple. Use it when ANY of these conditions apply:

1. **New Feature Implementation**: Adding meaningful new functionality
   - Example: "Add a logout button" - where should it go? What should happen on click?
   - Example: "Add form validation" - what rules? What error messages?

2. **Multiple Valid Approaches**: The task can be solved in several different ways
   - Example: "Add caching to the API" - could use Redis, in-memory, file-based, etc.
   - Example: "Improve performance" - many optimization strategies possible

3. **Code Modifications**: Changes that affect existing behavior or structure
   - Example: "Update the login flow" - what exactly should change?
   - Example: "Refactor this component" - what's the target architecture?

4. **Architectural Decisions**: The task requires choosing between patterns or technologies
   - Example: "Add real-time updates" - WebSockets vs SSE vs polling
   - Example: "Implement state management" - Redux vs Context vs custom solution

5. **Multi-File Changes**: The task will likely touch more than 2-3 files
   - Example: "Refactor the authentication system"
   - Example: "Add a new API endpoint with tests"

6. **Unclear Requirements**: You need to explore before understanding the full scope
   - Example: "Make the app faster" - need to profile and identify bottlenecks
   - Example: "Fix the bug in checkout" - need to investigate root cause

7. **User Preferences Matter**: The implementation could reasonably go multiple ways
   - If you would use AskUserQuestion to clarify the approach, use EnterPlanMode instead
   - Plan mode lets you explore first, then present options with context

## When NOT to Use This Tool

Only skip EnterPlanMode for simple tasks:
- Single-line or few-line fixes (typos, obvious bugs, small tweaks)
- Adding a single function with clear requirements
- Tasks where the user has given very specific, detailed instructions
- Pure research/exploration tasks (use the Agent tool instead)

## What Happens in Plan Mode

In plan mode, you'll:
1. Thoroughly explore the codebase using `find`/Glob, `grep`/Grep, and Read
2. Understand existing patterns and architecture
3. Design an implementation approach
4. Present your plan to the user for approval
5. Use AskUserQuestion if you need to clarify approaches
6. Exit plan mode with ExitPlanMode when ready to implement

## Examples

### GOOD - Use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Add user authentication to the app"
- Requires architectural decisions (session vs JWT, where to store tokens, middleware structure)

User: "Optimize the database queries"
- Multiple approaches possible, need to profile first, significant impact

User: "Implement dark mode"
- Architectural decision on theme system, affects many components

User: "Add a delete button to the user profile"
- Seems simple but involves: where to place it, confirmation dialog, API call, error handling, state updates

User: "Update the error handling in the API"
- Affects multiple files, user should approve the approach

### BAD - Don't use EnterPlanMode:
User: "Fix the typo in the README"
- Straightforward, no planning needed

User: "Add a console.log to debug this function"
- Simple, obvious implementation

User: "What files handle routing?"
- Research task, not implementation planning

## Important Notes

- This tool REQUIRES user approval - they must consent to entering plan mode
- If unsure whether to use it, err on the side of planning - it's better to get alignment upfront than to redo work
- Users appreciate being consulted before significant changes are made to their codebase

tools.name: EnterWorktree
tools.description:
Use this tool ONLY when explicitly instructed to work in a worktree — either by the user directly, or by project instructions (CLAUDE.md / memory). This tool creates an isolated git worktree and switches the current session into it.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly says "worktree" (e.g., "start a worktree", "work in a worktree", "create a worktree", "use a worktree")
- CLAUDE.md or memory instructions direct you to work in a worktree for the current task

## When NOT to Use

- The user asks to create a branch, switch branches, or work on a different branch — use git commands instead
- The user asks to fix a bug or work on a feature — use normal git workflow unless worktrees are explicitly requested by the user or project instructions
- Never use this tool unless "worktree" is explicitly mentioned by the user or in CLAUDE.md / memory instructions

## Requirements

- Must be in a git repository, OR have WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks configured in settings.json
- Must not already be in a worktree session when creating a new worktree (`name`); switching into another existing worktree via `path` is allowed

## Behavior

- In a git repository: creates a new git worktree inside `.claude/worktrees/` on a new branch. The base ref is governed by the `worktree.baseRef` setting: `fresh` (default) branches from origin/<default-branch>; `head` branches from your current local HEAD
- Outside a git repository: delegates to WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove hooks for VCS-agnostic isolation
- Switches the session's working directory to the new worktree
- Use ExitWorktree to leave the worktree mid-session (keep or remove). On session exit, if still in the worktree, the user will be prompted to keep or remove it

## Entering an existing worktree

Pass `path` instead of `name` to switch the session into a worktree that already exists (e.g., one you just created with `git worktree add`). On first entry from the launch directory, the path must appear in `git worktree list` for the repository that owns it — the current repository or, in a multi-repo workspace, a repository nested inside it; paths registered by neither are rejected. ExitWorktree will not remove a worktree entered this way; use `action: "keep"` to return to the original directory.

Switching with `path` also works when the session is already in a worktree (the previous worktree is left on disk, untouched, and only the new one is tracked for exit-time cleanup), and from agents whose working directory was pinned at launch (subagent isolation or explicit cwd). In both cases the target must be a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/` of the same repository, and from a pinned agent the switch only affects this agent, not the parent session. After a further switch, previously-visited worktrees are no longer writable — re-issue EnterWorktree with `path` to return to one.

## Parameters

- `name` (optional): A name for a new worktree. If neither `name` nor `path` is provided, a random name is generated.
- `path` (optional): Path to an existing worktree to enter instead of creating one — of the current repository, or (on first entry from the launch directory) of a repository nested inside it. Mutually exclusive with `name`.

tools.name: ExitPlanMode
tools.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

tools.name: ExitWorktree
tools.description:
Exit a worktree session created by EnterWorktree and return the session to the original working directory.

## Scope

This tool ONLY operates on worktrees created by EnterWorktree in this session. It will NOT touch:
- Worktrees you created manually with `git worktree add`
- Worktrees from a previous session (even if created by EnterWorktree then)
- The directory you're in if EnterWorktree was never called

If called outside an EnterWorktree session, the tool is a **no-op**: it reports that no worktree session is active and takes no action. Filesystem state is unchanged.

## When to Use

- The user explicitly asks to "exit the worktree", "leave the worktree", "go back", or otherwise end the worktree session
- Do NOT call this proactively — only when the user asks

## Parameters

- `action` (required): `"keep"` or `"remove"`
  - `"keep"` — leave the worktree directory and branch intact on disk. Use this if the user wants to come back to the work later, or if there are changes to preserve.
  - `"remove"` — delete the worktree directory and its branch. Use this for a clean exit when the work is done or abandoned.
- `discard_changes` (optional, default false): only meaningful with `action: "remove"`. If the worktree has uncommitted files or commits not on the original branch, the tool will REFUSE to remove it unless this is set to `true`. If the tool returns an error listing changes, confirm with the user before re-invoking with `discard_changes: true`.

## Behavior

- Restores the session's working directory to where it was before EnterWorktree
- Clears CWD-dependent caches (system prompt sections, memory files, plans directory) so the session state reflects the original directory
- If a tmux session was attached to the worktree: killed on `remove`, left running on `keep` (its name is returned so the user can reattach)
- Once exited, EnterWorktree can be called again to create a fresh worktree

Replaces, inserts, or deletes a single cell in a Jupyter notebook (.ipynb file).

Usage:
- You must use the Read tool on the notebook in this conversation before editing — this tool will fail otherwise.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use the default 5-minute Anthropic prompt-cache TTL. Sleeping past 300 seconds means the next wake-up reads your full conversation context uncached — slower and more expensive. So the natural breakpoints:

- **Under 5 minutes (60s–270s)**: cache stays warm. Right for actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about — a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue.
- **5 minutes to 1 hour (300s–3600s)**: pay the cache miss. Right when there's no point checking sooner — waiting on something that takes minutes to change, genuinely idle, or as the long fallback heartbeat when something else is the primary wake signal.

**Don't pick 300s.** It's the worst-of-both: you pay the cache miss without amortizing it. If you're tempted to "wait 5 minutes," either drop to 270s (stay in cache) or commit to 1200s+ (one cache miss buys a much longer wait). Don't think in round-number minutes — think in cache windows.

For idle ticks with no specific signal to watch, default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop checks back, you don't burn cache 12× per hour for nothing, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Think about what you're actually waiting for, not just "how long should I sleep." If you're polling a CI run that takes ~8 minutes, sleeping 60s burns the cache 8 times before it finishes — sleep ~270s twice instead.

The runtime clamps to [60, 3600], so you don't need to clamp yourself.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: SendMessage
tools.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.16)
2	project(amr_dispatcher_proto)
3	
4	# C++17 是硬性要求：
5	#   - protobuf 3.21 的 CMake 集成要求 17
6	#   - 本包的类型分发依赖 if constexpr（SILENT 分支）
7	set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
8	set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
9	
10	find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
11	find_package(rclcpp REQUIRED)
12	
13	# ament_get_python_install_dir() 提供 PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR，用于把 pybind11
14	# 扩展装到 site-packages（而不是 ROS 的可执行文件目录 lib/<pkg>）。
15	find_package(ament_cmake_python REQUIRED)
16	
17	# protobuf 用 CONFIG 模式优先，找不到再退回 MODULE。
18	# Ubuntu 24.04 / protobuf 3.21 装的是 Module 模式（FindProtobuf.cmake）。
19	# 若将来升级到 protobuf 4.x（开始提供 CONFIG 模式），这里仍然兼容。
20	find_package(Protobuf REQUIRED)
21	
22	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
23	# protobuf 代码生成
24	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
25	# 所有 proto 放在同一个 PROTO_PATH 下，互相 import 才能解析。
26	set(PROTO_SRC_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/proto)
27	
28	set(PROTO_FILES
29	  ${PROTO_SRC_DIR}/common.proto
30	  ${PROTO_SRC_DIR}/chassis.proto
31	  ${PROTO_SRC_DIR}/dispatcher.proto
32	  ${PROTO_SRC_DIR}/safety.proto
33	)
34	
35	# 生成到 build 目录，不污染源码树。
36	set(PROTO_GEN_DIR ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/generated)
37	file(MAKE_DIRECTORY ${PROTO_GEN_DIR})
38	
39	# 让构建期的 #include 路径与安装后的**逐字相同**。
40	#
41	# 问题：protoc 生成的 .pb.cc 之间用平铺名互相包含（`#include "common.pb.h"`），
42	# 而安装后位于 include/amr_dispatcher_proto/generated/common.pb.h。若下游包
43	# 按安装路径写 include，构建期就找不到；反之亦然——同一份头文件两套写法，
44	# 协作方必然记错。
45	#
46	# 解法：构建目录里造一个与安装同形的 include 根，用符号链接指回平铺目录。
47	# 于是 `amr_dispatcher_proto/generated/chassis.pb.h` 在构建期与安装后都成立，
48	# 且不产生第二份实体文件（不会出现两份头内容不一致的隐患）。
49	#
50	# 平台约束：项目仅支持 Linux（见 docker/Dockerfile.jazzy），符号链接可用。
51	set(PROTO_INCLUDE_ROOT ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/include)
52	file(MAKE_DIRECTORY ${PROTO_INCLUDE_ROOT}/amr_dispatcher_proto)
53	file(CREATE_LINK ${PROTO_GEN_DIR}
54	  ${PROTO_INCLUDE_ROOT}/amr_dispatcher_proto/generated
55	  SYMBOLIC)
56	
57	set(PROTO_GENERATED_SRCS)
58	set(PROTO_GENERATED_HDRS)
59	
60	foreach(proto_file ${PROTO_FILES})
61	  get_filename_component(proto_name ${proto_file} NAME_WE)
62	
63	  set(gen_src ${PROTO_GEN_DIR}/${proto_name}.pb.cc)
64	  set(gen_hdr ${PROTO_GEN_DIR}/${proto_name}.pb.h)
65	
66	  # DEPENDS 里要带上 common.proto：其余文件都 import 它，
67	  # 否则增量构建时可能先编 chassis.pb.cc 再生成 common.pb.h，导致找不到头文件。
68	  add_custom_command(
69	    OUTPUT ${gen_src} ${gen_hdr}
70	    COMMAND ${Protobuf_PROTOC_EXECUTABLE}
71	      --cpp_out=${PROTO_GEN_DIR}
72	      --proto_path=${PROTO_SRC_DIR}
73	      ${proto_file}
74	    DEPENDS ${proto_file} ${PROTO_SRC_DIR}/common.proto
75	    COMMENT "Generating C++ from ${proto_name}.proto"
76	    VERBATIM
77	  )
78	
79	  list(APPEND PROTO_GENERATED_SRCS ${gen_src})
80	  list(APPEND PROTO_GENERATED_HDRS ${gen_hdr})
81	endforeach()
82	
83	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
84	# 库：proto 消息 + typesupport 头文件
85	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
86	add_library(${PROJECT_NAME} SHARED
87	  ${PROTO_GENERATED_SRCS}
88	)
89	
90	target_include_directories(${PROJECT_NAME} PUBLIC
91	  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
92	  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${PROTO_INCLUDE_ROOT}>
93	  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include>
94	)
95	
96	# typesupport 头里用到 fastcdr（CDR 编解码）、rcutils（sha256）、
97	# rosidl_runtime_c（type hash / description 结构体）。
98	target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PUBLIC
99	  ${Protobuf_LIBRARIES}
100	  fastcdr
101	  rcutils::rcutils
102	  rosidl_runtime_c::rosidl_runtime_c
103	)
104	
105	target_link_libraries(${PROJECT_NAME} PUBLIC
106	  rosidl_typesupport_cpp::rosidl_typesupport_cpp
107	  rosidl_typesupport_fastrtps_cpp::rosidl_typesupport_fastrtps_cpp
108	  rosidl_typesupport_introspection_cpp::rosidl_typesupport_introspection_cpp
109	)
110	
111	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
112	# 描述符集 + typesupport 绑定生成
113	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
114	# 描述符集是 protoc 解析结果的权威序列化，供两处使用：
115	#   1) 生成 typesupport 绑定清单（本文件下方）
116	#   2) Python CLI 运行期构建描述符池（避免 CLI 依赖 protoc 可执行文件）
117	set(PROTO_DESCRIPTOR_SET ${PROTO_GEN_DIR}/descriptors.pb)
118	
119	add_custom_command(
120	  OUTPUT ${PROTO_DESCRIPTOR_SET}
121	  COMMAND ${Protobuf_PROTOC_EXECUTABLE}
122	    --descriptor_set_out=${PROTO_DESCRIPTOR_SET}
123	    --include_imports
124	    --proto_path=${PROTO_SRC_DIR}
125	    ${PROTO_FILES}
126	  DEPENDS ${PROTO_FILES}
127	  COMMENT "Generating protobuf descriptor set"
128	  VERBATIM
129	)
130	
131	# 从描述符集生成绑定清单。用 Python 而非正则，是为了正确处理嵌套消息。
132	set(TYPESUPPORT_INC ${PROTO_GEN_DIR}/proto_typesupport_registry.inc)
133	
134	# Development 组件提供 Python3_INCLUDE_DIRS / Python3_LIBRARIES，
135	# pybind11 模块编译需要。
136	find_package(Python3 COMPONENTS Interpreter Development REQUIRED)
137	
138	# Python 扩展模块的后缀，形如 .cpython-312-x86_64-linux-gnu.so。
139	# 不用 Python3_SOABI_SUFFIX——那不是标准变量。直接从解释器问：
140	#   sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX')
141	execute_process(
142	  COMMAND ${Python3_EXECUTABLE} -c
143	    "import sysconfig; print(sysconfig.get_config_var('EXT_SUFFIX') or '.so')"
144	  OUTPUT_VARIABLE Python3_EXT_SUFFIX
145	  OUTPUT_STRIP_TRAILING_WHITESPACE
146	)
147	
148	add_custom_command(
149	  OUTPUT ${TYPESUPPORT_INC}
150	  COMMAND ${Python3_EXECUTABLE}
151	    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/scripts/gen_typesupport_bindings.py
152	    ${PROTO_DESCRIPTOR_SET}
153	    ${TYPESUPPORT_INC}
154	  DEPENDS ${PROTO_DESCRIPTOR_SET}
155	    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/scripts/gen_typesupport_bindings.py
156	  COMMENT "Generating typesupport bindings"
157	  VERBATIM
158	)
159	
160	# 描述符集也要安装：Python CLI 运行期用它构建描述符池，
161	# 这样 CLI 不依赖运行环境里是否有 protoc。
162	install(
163	  FILES ${PROTO_DESCRIPTOR_SET}
164	  DESTINATION share/${PROJECT_NAME}/proto
165	)
166	
167	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
168	# Python 扩展：把 typesupport handle 以 PyCapsule 暴露给 rclpy
169	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
170	# 存在理由：rclpy 的 C 扩展要求 _TYPE_SUPPORT 是 PyCapsule，而 protobuf
171	# 类型没有 rosidl_generator_py 生成物。详见 src/py_typesupport_module.cpp。
172	find_package(pybind11 QUIET)
173
